# One-Sentence Summary

FarmCPU alternates fixed and random effect components for genome-wide
association analysis and is commonly used as one of several model options in
plant and other GWAS workflows.

# Scope for simitall

Use as a comparative GWAS analysis method after simulation, with the same
filters, covariates, samples, and causal-truth benchmark used for the baseline
mixed-model analysis.

# Agent-Safe Takeaways

- Compare FarmCPU with a prespecified baseline such as MLM rather than choosing
  a method after viewing significance results.
- Use simulation truth to compare calibration, recovery, and false positives.
- Preserve population structure and relatedness handling in every comparison.

# Limitations and Guardrails

A method's performance varies with marker density, LD, sample size, trait
architecture, and structure. More detected markers are not automatically a
better or more biologically valid result.
